ca_other_routes.blurb: A scatter of boulders high on Mt. San Antonio (Baldy) in the Angeles National Forest, at roughly 8,300 feet, sitting in the boulder field beneath the bowl below the summit. The fifteen problems here are mostly short sit-starts, running from very easy up to V4, with the bulk around V1, so it suits newer boulderers and warm-up sessions. Landings are often over sharp, broken rock, so bring one or two pads. Getting here means a long hike up a popular trail past the old ski hut, but the altitude keeps temperatures cool in summer and the views are the reward.

ca_brownie_girl_dome.blurb: A brown-faced dome in the north end of Joshua Tree's Wonderland of Rocks, the first sizeable formation along the trail toward Willow Hole. Fifteen routes, mostly traditional with a few top-rope lines, spread from easy fifth class through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, with a handful of harder ones up to the low 5.12 range. The west face has some pleasant dike climbing. It is a short walk in, around a quarter hour, which makes it handy for a quick half day of moderate crack and face routes with the occasional bold move.

ca_gibraltar_rock.blurb: A compact sandstone formation beside Gibraltar Road in the Santa Ynez foothills above Santa Barbara, with a view over the city from the top. Most of the fifteen routes are traditional, with a few bolted lines and a single top-rope option, spanning easy 5.6 terrain through to the low 5.12 range and clustering around the middle and upper grades. Approaches are short from the road, and several easier lines suit a top-rope set up for newer climbers. Fall through spring gives the most comfortable conditions, and the sunnier south and southwest sides are better saved for cooler hours.

ca_little_lebowski_urban_achievers_crag.blurb: The largest of the three sub-areas at The Playground, a small sport climbing zone in the hills above Santa Barbara. Roughly a dozen well-bolted routes on short, friable rock face both north and south, and most can also be top-roped. Grades run from easy 5.6 to the low 5.12 range, with the majority between 5.8 and 5.11, plus one boulder problem. The walk in takes about half an hour and includes some brush, which keeps crowds thin, so you often have it to yourself. Good for a relaxed day of moderate sport routes.

ca_cereal_cliff.blurb: A small cliff in the Hidden Valley part of Joshua Tree's roadside rocks, set northwest of The Hot Tub and visible from the pullout on the road. Its sections face in several directions, including toward the road to the south, west and north, so shade is easy to find. The fifteen routes are mostly traditional with a couple of top-rope lines, from easy fifth class to about 5.11, with the largest group around 5.8. The routes are short, many on a brown varnished buttress, with a few thin spots where protection is sparse. A convenient stop for a quick lap or two.

ca_lower_lunchbox_area.blurb: The main cluster of climbing in the Lunchbox section of the Hospital Rock cliffs in Sequoia National Park, at about 2,900 feet above the Middle Fork of the Kaweah. These short quartzite routes are nearly all traditional, with one top-rope line, and the grades run from an easy scramble and 5.4 through the 5.8 range up to a few 5.10s and 5.11s. A climbers' trail leaves the river trail near the parking lot, so the walk is brief. The wider Hospital Rock area is usually uncrowded and tolerable for most of the year, and makes a handy alternative when higher rock is out of condition.
